free_tier.stated: Three SX models, all with SATA HDD plus NVMe. SX65: 4 x 16 TB up to 4 x 22 TB SATA, 2 x 1 TB NVMe, 128 GB DDR4 ECC, Ryzen 7 3700X, from EUR 84.00 to EUR 159.00/month excl. VAT, EUR 39.00 one-time setup. SX135: 8 x 16 TB up to 8 x 22 TB, 2 x 1.92 TB NVMe, 256 GB, Ryzen 9 3900, EUR 289.00 to EUR 309.00/month, EUR 144.00 setup. SX295: 14 x 22 TB SATA (308 TB), 2 x 7.68 TB NVMe, EPYC 7502P, EUR 599.00 to EUR 879.00/month, EUR 439.00 setup. Traffic is unlimited and the port is 1 Gbit/s.

egress.terms: unlimited and free of charge on the 1 Gbit/s port; over 20 TB is charged at EUR 1.00/TB only on servers with the 10G uplink addon

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: a dedicated server with root, rescue system, VNC install and an installimage script; rsync, rclone, ssh, NFS and MinIO all run on it
chaining: 308 TB for EUR 599.00 a month is the largest single machine and the cheapest per terabyte at that size. It is the only row that covers the 20 TiB archive on one invoice with room for the hot set

limits.value: Traffic is unlimited and free of charge and the port is 1 Gbit/s, so throughput is the wall, not a byte allowance. The page adds that the unlimited policy does not apply to servers with the 10G uplink addon, where usage over 20 TB is charged at EUR 1.00/TB.

evidence.proved: spec table quoted: 'SATA HDD 4x 16 TB up to 4x 22 TB SATA | 8x 16 TB up to 8x 22 TB SATA | 14x 22 TB SATA', 'NVMe SSD 2x 1 TB | 2x 1.92 TB | 2x 7.68 TB', 'RAM 128 GB DDR4 ECC | 256 GB DDR4 ECC reg.', 'Connection 1 GBit/s-Port', 'Traffic Unlimited'

card prices quoted: SX65 'EUR 159.00 per month' and 'EUR 84.00 per month' with 'EUR 39.00 one-time setup fee'; SX135 'EUR 309.00' and 'EUR 289.00' with 'EUR 144.00'; SX295 'EUR 599.00' and 'EUR 879.00' with 'EUR 439.00'
the hero text states 'SX server with up to 15.36 TB NVMe SSD and 308 TB SATA HDD', which is the 14 x 22 TB configuration of SX295

notes: The two prices per card are read as a low and a high configuration of the same model, because the card says '3 Types' for SX65 and '1 Type' for SX295, but the page never prints a price beside a disk count. A per-TB figure for SX65 or SX135 would therefore be an inference about which price pairs with which drive set, so only SX295 is given one. Hetzner also sells a Storage Box on the same page at EUR 3.20/TB (1 TB), EUR 10.90 (5 TB), EUR 20.80 (10 TB) and EUR 40.60 (20 TB); that is a managed NAS product, not a rented machine, and it is out of this document's scope.
